patch_description: The best prior program (score 0.99, ratio 0.24) started from an icosahedron + 2 polar points and used an annealed soft objective followed by greedy coordinate descent. The current program's D6 double-ring family gets stuck at ratio 0.22 (score 0.92). I therefore replace the main construction with: (1) an icosahedron-plus-poles initialization (also compared against the D6 parametric optimum so we never regress), (2) the existing annealed soft-min/soft-max `polish`, and (3) a greedy coordinate descent on the exact ratio with adaptive per-point step sizes as recommended: binding points (those in the min-distance and max-distance pairs) get larger steps (0.05–0.1) while non-binding points get small steps (0.01), concentrating the 14×3×2 sweep budget on coordinates that actually affect the binding constraints. This preserves the exact-ratio convergence of the greedy stage while cutting wasted evaluations and improving the achievable ratio.
